title: A Mosque of Harm and a True Bargain

paragraphs.text: Some bedouins believe and see their spending as a way to come near Allah. He will admit them to His mercy. The first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and those who followed them well, are pleased with Allah, and He with them. Some around Madinah are hypocrites whom only Allah knows. Others admit their sins, mixing good and bad deeds. Perhaps Allah will forgive them.
Take charity from their wealth to purify them. Pray for them. Allah accepts repentance and charity. Say, "Do your deeds; Allah will see them." Others must wait for Allah's decision.

Some hypocrites built a mosque to cause harm and division. Never pray in it. A mosque built on righteousness from the first day is more worthy. A building on righteousness is better than one on the edge of a bank about to collapse.

Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth in return for Paradise. This true promise is in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. Believers repent, worship, praise, bow, and prostrate. They should not ask forgiveness for polytheists, even relatives. Abraham did so for his father only because of a promise. Abraham was compassionate and patient.

hardWords.m: the first ones to go ahead
